D.t: Cinde Warmington trails by 9.7 and wins 6% of simulations. Closing it takes about 33,257 voters switching sides, or 66,514 more net votes from new turnout.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between R +17.8 and R +1.7. Only an unusual polling error changes the winner.
The polls page average is R +10.2. Your best recent poll is University of New Hampshire at R +3.7; your worst is National Public Affairs at R +15.1. 6 polls in the last 30 days.

The biggest vote banks for Democrats: Grafton, a projected net 3,945 votes; Cheshire, a projected net 989 votes; Strafford, a projected net 367 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: Hillsborough, R +11.9, 28.3% of the vote; Rockingham, R +11.5, 24.4% of the vote; Merrimack, R +8.5, 11.3% of the vote; Strafford, D +0.6, 9.3% of the vote.

D.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
D.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Cinde Warmington runs furthest behind in Belknap, Carroll, Sullivan. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: White voters, 91% of voters, 42 to 56, where a 5 point gain is worth 4.56 points; Voters who cast ballots in 2022 and 2024, 72% of voters, 46 to 52, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.62 points; Voters who find daily costs hard to afford, 60% of voters, 49 to 48, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.02 points.

The forecast's worst groups for Cinde Warmington: Immigration voters 19 to 78, Voters who can afford daily costs 33 to 64, 2024 nonvoters and third party voters 37 to 59. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
$400K cash against $2.6M. Outspent: lean on earned media, digital, field and the outside groups, and pick the two or three media markets that decide it.

D.h: What the ballots so far say
D.t: The early vote has moved this forecast 0.1 points toward Cinde Warmington. Bank it: chase the remaining mail ballots and low propensity voters who have not voted.
Cash: $2.6M in the bank against $400K for Cinde Warmington.

R.t: Kelly Ayotte leads by 9.7 in the forecast and wins 94% of simulations. The cushion is about 66,514 votes; a one point swing is about 3,446 voters changing sides.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between R +1.7 and R +17.8. Only an unusual polling error changes the winner.
The polls page average is R +10.2. Your best recent poll is National Public Affairs at R +15.1; your worst is University of New Hampshire at R +3.7. 6 polls in the last 30 days.

The biggest vote banks for Republicans: Hillsborough, a projected net 23,278 votes; Rockingham, a projected net 19,395 votes; Belknap, a projected net 10,632 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: Hillsborough, R +11.9, 28.3% of the vote; Rockingham, R +11.5, 24.4% of the vote; Merrimack, R +8.5, 11.3% of the vote; Strafford, D +0.6, 9.3% of the vote.

R.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
R.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Kelly Ayotte runs furthest behind in Cheshire, Rockingham, Coos. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: White voters, 91% of voters, 56 to 42, where a 5 point gain is worth 4.56 points; Voters who cast ballots in 2022 and 2024, 72% of voters, 52 to 46, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.62 points; Voters who find daily costs hard to afford, 60% of voters, 48 to 49, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.02 points.

The forecast's worst groups for Kelly Ayotte: Asian and other voters 27 to 70, Health care and Social Security voters 35 to 63, Corruption voters 44 to 54. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
$2.6M cash against $400K. Spend it early on persuasion television in the battleground counties and keep a reserve for the last week.

R.h: What the ballots so far say
R.t: The early vote has moved this forecast 0.1 points away from Kelly Ayotte. Election Day has to make it up: the remaining vote must break harder your way than the forecast expects.
